ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #3 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is inferring the meaning of a word? (1 mark)
   A. Working out its meaning from the words around it
   B. Ignoring it
   C. Copying it
   D. Spelling it backwards

2. Which conjunction gives a choice? (1 mark)
   A. yet
   B. and
   C. or
   D. so

3. Which conjunction shows a result? 'The floor was dirty, ____ we mopped it.' (1 mark)
   A. yet
   B. nor
   C. so
   D. or

4. Which word means 'the leader of a team'? (1 mark)
   A. whistle
   B. captain
   C. stadium
   D. kit

5. What is a digital text? (1 mark)
   A. A text printed on paper only
   B. A hand-written letter
   C. A text read on a screen
   D. A spoken poem

6. Which key words would help you find out how netball is played? (1 mark)
   A. password
   B. netball rules for children
   C. my address
   D. free prizes

7. Which question word asks about a thing or an action? (1 mark)
   A. whose
   B. where
   C. when
   D. what

8. Which sentence uses the correct word? (1 mark)
   A. I noe the answer.
   B. I know the answer.
   C. I no the answer.
   D. I nose the answer.

9. Which word begins with the cluster 'pr'? (1 mark)
   A. protect
   B. clap
   C. brush
   D. grow

10. What is rhythm? (1 mark)
   A. The beat in the words
   B. The colour of the page
   C. The title
   D. The number of lines

11. When I arrived, the bus had left. Which happened first? (1 mark)
   A. I arrived.
   B. Both together.
   C. Neither happened.
   D. The bus left.

12. Which sentence uses the correct form of the verb 'go' with the present perfect? (1 mark)
   A. They have gone to the river.
   B. They have went to the river.
   C. They have go to the river.
   D. They has gone to the river.

13. Which is a good way to start a diary entry sentence? (1 mark)
   A. Today I ...
   B. Chapter One ...
   C. Dear Sir ...
   D. Yours faithfully ...

14. What is a good way to end a diary entry? (1 mark)
   A. With a plan for tomorrow or a short sign-off
   B. With a map
   C. With a list of prices
   D. With a poem only

15. What is a fine? (1 mark)
   A. A gift of money
   B. A payment for a service
   C. Money paid as a punishment for breaking a rule
   D. A kind of salary

16. Which page of a magazine lists the articles and their page numbers? (1 mark)
   A. The cover
   B. The advert page
   C. The contents page
   D. The comic page

17. What does 'skimming' mean? (1 mark)
   A. Reading quickly to get the main idea
   B. Copying a passage
   C. Reading backwards
   D. Looking for one number

18. Which preposition completes: 'The clock is ____ the door.' (higher than, not touching)? (1 mark)
   A. under
   B. above
   C. below
   D. behind

19. Which word has a double consonant? (1 mark)
   A. paper
   B. river
   C. letter
   D. later

20. Which is the correct -ing form of 'sit'? (1 mark)
   A. siting
   B. sitting
   C. sittting
   D. siteing

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Write the minimal pairs for: ship, seat, sock. (3 marks)

22. Explain the difference between a fact and an opinion, with an example of each. (3 marks)

23. What kind of person is Kamau in 'The Clean-Up Day'? Give a reason from the text. (3 marks)

24. Name the five senses and say why a descriptive writer uses them. (3 marks)

25. Correct the spellings: peple, libary, beutiful. (3 marks)

26. Name three parts of a newspaper. (3 marks)

27. Explain the difference between 'in' and 'into'. Give one sentence for each. (3 marks)

28. Explain the difference in meaning between 'hopping' and 'hoping'. Use each in a sentence. (3 marks)

29. Write the steps you would follow to search for information safely online. (4 marks)

30. Rewrite using the past perfect: 'The bus left. Then I arrived.' (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #3 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Working out its meaning from the words around it
   Context gives clues.

2. C — or
   'Or' offers choices.

3. C — so
   'So' shows result.

4. B — captain
   The captain leads the team.

5. C — A text read on a screen
   Digital texts are read on phones, tablets and computers.

6. B — netball rules for children
   Good key words describe the topic you want.

7. D — what
   'What' asks about things, ideas and actions.

8. B — I know the answer.
   'Know' means to have learnt something.

9. A — protect
   'Protect' begins with p and r.

10. A — The beat in the words
   Rhythm is the pattern of beats.

11. D — The bus left.
   The past perfect shows the earlier action.

12. A — They have gone to the river.
   The participle of go is gone.

13. A — Today I ...
   Diary sentences often start with 'Today I ...'.

14. A — With a plan for tomorrow or a short sign-off
   Diaries often end with plans or 'Goodnight'.

15. C — Money paid as a punishment for breaking a rule
   Fines punish law breaking.

16. C — The contents page
   The contents page shows where to find each article.

17. A — Reading quickly to get the main idea
   Skimming gives the gist.

18. B — above
   'Above' means higher than.

19. C — letter
   'Letter' has a double t.

20. B — sitting
   Sit doubles the t.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: ship and sheep (or sip); seat and sheet (or sit); sock and shock.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct partner word.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: A fact can be checked, such as 'The club meets on Fridays.' An opinion is what someone thinks, such as 'Saving is a good idea.'
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for examples.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: Observant and responsible: he noticed a hole in the fence and said it should be fixed at once.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each quality and 1 for evidence.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sight, sound, smell, touch and taste. They help the reader to imagine the thing being described.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the senses and 1 for the reason.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: people, library, beautiful
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Masthead (name), headline, byline, article, picture, caption, advert, weather report (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: 'In' shows where something is: The coins are in the box. 'Into' shows movement to the inside: She put the coins into the box.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for examples.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: 'Hopping' means jumping, for example 'The rabbit is hopping.' 'Hoping' means wishing, for example 'I am hoping to win.'
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for both sentences.

29. (4 marks)
   Answer: Decide what to find out; choose key words; use an approved site; read carefully and note the facts in your own words.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: The bus had left before I arrived. (Or: When I arrived, the bus had left.)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 'had left' and 1 for the linking word.
